subsystems.name: Radioisotope source
subsystems.role: supplies the energy: carbon-14 (or tritium) that decays and emits beta particles for years or thousands of years.

subsystems.name: Diamond betavoltaic converter
subsystems.role: turns beta particles into electricity, like a solar cell that runs on electrons instead of photons.

subsystems.name: Encapsulation
subsystems.role: contains the radioisotope and stops beta particles, which travel only a short distance in solid matter.

subsystems.name: Power conditioning
subsystems.role: stacks and buffers the tiny trickle of current so a sensor can draw short bursts.
parts: solid-state buffer capacitor or thin-film battery

subsystems.name: Sensor and radio
subsystems.role: does the actual job of measuring and reporting.

buildSteps.title: Recover carbon-14
buildSteps.detail: Irradiated graphite moderator blocks from retired gas-cooled reactors are the main source; the carbon-14 is chemically separated and converted into a methane-like precursor gas.

buildSteps.title: Grow diamond by CVD
buildSteps.detail: The carbon-14 gas is fed into a plasma reactor, where carbon atoms deposit atom-by-atom onto a seed substrate, building synthetic diamond. Because the feedstock is radioactive, the reactor must be a contained facility.

buildSteps.title: Dope the layers
buildSteps.detail: Boron and phosphorus are added during growth to create p-type and n-type diamond, forming the p-i-n diode that separates the freed electrons from their holes.

buildSteps.title: Metallise and cut
buildSteps.detail: Contacts are patterned onto the faces, and the wafer is cut into individual cells.

buildSteps.title: Encapsulate the isotope
buildSteps.detail: The radioactive diamond is capped with a further layer of non-radioactive diamond so beta particles are absorbed inside the package.

buildSteps.title: Test the cell
buildSteps.detail: Open-circuit voltage and short-circuit current are measured over months to confirm output holds steady as decay proceeds.

buildSteps.title: Integrate the node
buildSteps.detail: Cells are wired to a buffer capacitor and the sensor board, then the radio duty cycle is tuned to the power budget.

buildSteps.title: Qualify for the field
buildSteps.detail: Sealed-source safety approval, leak and temperature cycling tests precede any deployment.

prerequisites.why: tritium-powered cells are already sold for niche, very-low-power uses; the principle is proven.
p- and n-type diamond diodes exist in laboratories but are far from ordinary commercial wafer processing.
the feedstock is abundant in decommissioning stockpiles, but separation has only been done at research scale.
microcontrollers that sleep on microwatts make a self-powered node conceivable at all.
radioactive devices must be licensed, transported and disposed of under existing nuclear rules.

pathway.milestone: a first carbon-14 diamond battery demonstrated in the UK in 2024, producing microwatts
pathway.unlocks: proof that a diamond cell can run for decades without charging.

pathway.milestone: cell-plus-buffer nodes piloted where battery replacement is impossible or costly
pathway.unlocks: sensors in decommissioning sites, pipelines, downhole tools and remote infrastructure.

pathway.milestone: tuning radios and duty cycles to a microwatt budget
pathway.unlocks: occasional reporting rather than continuous streaming — the honest limit of this power source.

pathway.milestone: medically approved implants and mass-produced cells
pathway.unlocks: decades-long monitoring inside the body or in sealed equipment, if safety and cost allow.
